title: Stocks measure how brave people feel
hook: Why do stocks sometimes rise on bad news about the economy?
metaphor: Lending to a lemonade stand gets you fixed interest. Owning a slice gets you a share of the profits. One is safe, one is hopeful.
body: A share is a slice of a real company and its future profits.
An index like the S&P 500 is a slice of five hundred of them.
People buy shares when they feel brave and money is easy to get.
So stocks track confidence and available cash more than today's economy.

caveat: A handful of giant companies can carry a whole index. The average share may be doing something else.
